nodes.label: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
nodes.desc: Jurist, economist, social reformer and chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution of India (1891-1956).

nodes.label: Constitution of India
nodes.desc: Adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.

nodes.label: Drafting Committee
nodes.desc: Committee of the Constituent Assembly that prepared the Draft Constitution; he was elected its chairman in August 1947.

nodes.label: Constituent Assembly
nodes.desc: The body that framed the Constitution of India between 1946 and 1949.

nodes.label: Article 32
nodes.desc: The right to constitutional remedies. He described it in the Assembly as the heart and soul of the Constitution.

nodes.label: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
nodes.desc: President of the Constituent Assembly.

nodes.label: Mahatma Gandhi
nodes.desc: Co-signatory of the Poona Pact of 1932.

nodes.label: Poona Pact (1932)
nodes.desc: Agreement replacing separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.

nodes.label: Round Table Conferences
nodes.desc: Conferences in London (1930-1932) on India's constitutional future, where he represented the depressed classes.

nodes.label: Mahad Satyagraha (1927)
nodes.desc: Movement asserting the right to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank at Mahad.

nodes.label: Kalaram Temple Satyagraha
nodes.desc: Temple entry movement at Nashik launched in 1930.

nodes.label: Annihilation of Caste (1936)
nodes.desc: His best-known critique of the caste system, prepared as an address and published in 1936.

nodes.label: Castes in India (1916)
nodes.desc: Paper presented at Columbia University on the mechanism, genesis and development of caste.

nodes.label: The Problem of the Rupee (1923)
nodes.desc: His doctoral thesis at the London School of Economics on Indian currency.

nodes.label: Who Were the Shudras? (1946)
nodes.desc: A historical study of the origins of the Shudras.

nodes.label: The Buddha and His Dhamma (1957)
nodes.desc: His final work, published after his death.

nodes.label: Mooknayak
nodes.desc: Marathi fortnightly he started in 1920.

nodes.label: Columbia University
nodes.desc: Where he studied from 1913 and later received an honorary doctorate (1952).

nodes.label: London School of Economics
nodes.desc: Where he earned his D.Sc. in economics.

nodes.label: Sayajirao Gaekwad III
nodes.desc: Maharaja of Baroda, whose scholarship funded his studies at Columbia.

nodes.label: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
nodes.desc: Organisation he founded in 1924 for the education and welfare of the depressed classes.

nodes.label: Independent Labour Party
nodes.desc: Political party he founded in 1936.

nodes.label: Scheduled Castes Federation
nodes.desc: All India Scheduled Castes Federation, founded in 1942.

nodes.label: People's Education Society
nodes.desc: Educational society he founded in 1945; it opened Siddharth College in 1946.

nodes.label: Hindu Code Bill
nodes.desc: Legislation reforming Hindu personal law that he championed as Law Minister.

nodes.label: Dhamma Deeksha, Nagpur (1956)
nodes.desc: His embrace of Buddhism on 14 October 1956.

nodes.label: Social democracy
nodes.desc: Liberty, equality and fraternity as principles of life, a central theme of his closing speech in the Constituent Assembly.
